goal: Score creativity of a 2-sentence rewrite vs its anchor. scorer(text, anchor) -> float in [0,1]. Correct on a pair when score(more_creative) > score(less_creative).
fitness: SEP = mean(score over positives) - mean(score over negatives) on train; both distributions reported; selection (SEP, acc, -sd_margin).
contract: Complete importable Python module exposing METRICS={name:fn}. Deterministic, values ALWAYS in [0,1] via principled squashing calibrated on REFERENCE stats (e.g. wordfreq lexicon), never on eval pairs. Allowed imports: wordfreq, numpy, scipy, sklearn, re, math, collections, statistics. Downloads BLOCKED. NO hand-typed content word lists (max 40 content tokens in literals; >=3 rare train-text tokens = auto-reject).
novelty_criteria: Accepted as NOVEL only if: (1) |pearson r| of per-pair margin vector vs EVERY incumbent < 0.6; (2) it measures an uncovered/weakly-covered causal node with a real named mechanism; (3) leakage-clean.

nodes.definition: Human judgment of how creative a text is (Consensual Assessment Technique / Likert).
Originality / statistical rarity of the idea or expression relative to a reference population.
Effectiveness / fit: coherent, relevant, satisfying task constraints. Second necessary criterion.
Embedding-space distance between concepts co-present in the text (SemDis; DSI = mean pairwise distance over all words).
Negative log probability of words given context under a language model; inverse of contextual predictability.
Freshness of figurative expressions vs conventional/dead metaphor; aptness is the paired appropriateness condition.
Proportion of text built from high-frequency collocations, formulaic sequences, stock phrases.
Use of low-corpus-frequency words relative to norms.
Tangibility / mental-image evocation of the words used (norm-based).
Amount of descriptive development added to the core idea (TTCT elaboration).
Internal consistency and topical unity; global coherence matters more than local transitions.
Type-token ratio. Weak and possibly INVERSE relation to judged creative quality; unreliable on 2-sentence texts.
Capacity to connect distant concepts (Mednick flat associative hierarchies); observable footprint IS semantic_distance.
Word frequency confounds surprisal-based novelty estimates: rarity inflates surprisal without conceptual novelty.

edges.evidence: One of two necessary criteria in the standard definition.
Wundt curve: preference and judged creativity peak at moderate novelty; maximal surprise reads as bizarre.
Novelty without appropriateness is judged bizarre, not creative (random condition: high novelty, low creativity).
Creativity requires BOTH; appropriateness moderates the effect of novelty (adding appropriateness to unoriginal ideas can even lower ratings).
edges.source: Diedrich et al.; Rastelli et al. 2022

edges.evidence: SemDis distances predict human originality ratings; DAT pairwise distance correlates with creativity batteries.
BERT-based DSI explains up to 72% of variance in human creativity ratings of short narratives.
LM surprisal moderately correlates with human novelty judgments of metaphors.
Frequency is a stronger, partly independent predictor: surprisal partly re-encodes lexical rarity.
Formulaic sequences are by definition high-frequency conventional co-occurrences.
High predictability from clichéd constructions associates with lower quality/creativity scores.
Novel metaphors require online meaning construction (N400/LPC evidence) — the signature of new conceptual combination.
Aptness, not novelty alone, predicts positive quality ratings — mirrors novelty×appropriateness.
Rarer words associate with more original responses/higher-scored essays.
Rarity signals uncommon phrasing, not conceptual novelty — unreliable alone.
Some studies favor abstract sophistication, others vivid imagery; direction context-dependent.
TTCT scores elaboration; added detail raises expert quality judgments.
Incoherent text fails the appropriateness criterion regardless of novelty.
edges.source: Rastelli et al. 2022 (derived); TAACO quality studies

edges.evidence: Flat associative hierarchies produce remote associates; the textual footprint is distant concepts co-occurring.
One study found inverse TTR-creativity correlation; treat as caution against rewarding vocabulary spread per se.

load_bearing_paths: semantic_distance -> novelty -> judged_creativity (strongest measured path; DSI explains up to 72% variance)
cliche_formulaicity -> novelty(-) AND predictability -> judged_creativity(-) (the anti-creativity signal)
coherence -> appropriateness -> judged_creativity (the constraint side: novelty only counts when this holds)
novelty x appropriateness -> judged_creativity is CONJUNCTIVE: scorers should combine the two sides multiplicatively or with a gate, not additively
surprisal/lexical_rarity -> novelty are CONFOUNDED with each other via word frequency: a scorer should not double-count rarity and surprise as independent evidence

population_stats.mechanism: Varied alignment-block structure (entropy of difflib opcode block sizes) gated by mean surprisal of changed content tokens. Structural diversity alone is cheap (just reorder/replace); structural diversity with novel content signals real creative elaboration. Avoids word-length inversion by making signal structural, gate lexical.

Information density capped at outlier threshold: reward high-surprisal text, but penalize when surprisal reaches extreme outliers (>3 SDs from reference). Legitimate elaborations add informative words; nonsense elaborations cluster rare/extreme words. Identifies inserted tokens via difflib; measures their surprisal distribution. Citation: Beaty & Johnson 2021 (DSI without extreme outliers); Kintsch et al. 1983 (parsing loads from extreme lexical rarity).

Surprisal of novel bigrams in text vs anchor (figurative/metaphorical signal) gated by absence of hedging markers (kind of, sort of, in a way, arguably, perhaps, seems, might be, somehow, possibly, allegedly, supposedly, more or less). Hedging language ruins appropriateness even with novel phrasing. Conjunctive: high novel-bigram surprisal × low hedge-frequency.
Token-sequence matching via difflib.SequenceMatcher (citation: Lempel-Ziv 1976 compression theory; applied to text elaboration novelty in DSI extensions, Beaty & Johnson 2021)
word n-gram TF-IDF divergence from anchor
Elaboration-to-substitution ratio: prefers texts where NEW content is inserted relative to word-swaps, via token-level difflib alignment and ratio gating.
Mean word length as morphological complexity proxy (Brysbaert et al. Concreteness Norms; Morphological Complexity Hypothesis: base roots are short/concrete, affixations are long/abstract)
Lexical overlap between adjacent sentences (TAACO Text Analysis Across Corpora; Rastelli et al. 2022 PNAS Nexus novelty x appropriateness; Graesser Coherence Research)
Spearman rank correlation of token position with per-token surprisal (citation: Nowak & Lewenstein 2002 on optimal complexity; temporal pacing in creativity theory per Csikszentmihalyi flow)

Shannon entropy of alignment-block SIZES from difflib.SequenceMatcher opcodes. Creative revisions have varied edit-block structure (insert/delete/replace at different scales); formulaic rewrites have uniform blocks. Lempel-Ziv (1976) compression theory; structural novelty in semantic distance improves elaboration signal. Calibrated via self-normalized entropy [0,1].
Bigram divergence from anchor (novelty) gated by lexical overlap with anchor (coherence). Conjunctive scoring implements novelty×appropriateness interaction per Rastelli et al. 2022.

Jensen-Shannon divergence of function-word category frequency ratios (pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, modals) between text and anchor. Formulaic sequences lock function-word patterns; creative rewrites break these locks. Citation: Gablasova et al. 2017 (formulaic sequences are frozen collocations); Sinclair 1991 (idiom principle).

Shannon entropy of per-token surprisal distribution; creative elaborations pace information novelty non-uniformly. Citation: Nowak & Lewenstein 2002 (optimal complexity theory); Csikszentmihalyi 1990 (flow states benefit from varied pacing). Calibrated on wordfreq lexicon reference surprisal stats.

champion.code:
import math
import re
import numpy as np
from wordfreq import word_frequency, top_n_list
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
import statistics

_W = re.compile(r"[a-zA-Z']+")
STOP = set(("a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my your "
    "his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may might must "
    "about into over under out up down off than too very just also").split())

def _toks(s):
    return [t for t in _W.findall((s or "").lower())]

def _content(s):
    return [t for t in _toks(s) if t not in STOP and len(t) > 1]

def _word_surprisal(word):
    p = word_frequency(word, "en")
    if p > 0:
        return -math.log2(p)
    return 24.0

def _ref_surprisal_stats():
    words = top_n_list("en", 50000)
    ps = np.array([word_frequency(w, "en") for w in words])
    ps = ps[ps > 0]
    ps = ps / ps.sum()
    sur = -np.log2(ps)
    mu = float((ps * sur).sum())
    sd = float(math.sqrt((ps * (sur - mu) ** 2).sum()))
    return mu, sd

_SURP_MU, _SURP_SD = _ref_surprisal_stats()

def structural_diversity_content_gated(text, anchor):
    if not (text and anchor):
        return 0.5
    anchor_toks = _content(anchor)
    text_toks = _content(text)
    if not text_toks or not anchor_toks:
        return 0.5
    matcher = SequenceMatcher(None, anchor_toks, text_toks)
    opcodes = matcher.get_opcodes()
    if not opcodes:
        return 0.5
    block_sizes = []
    changed_tokens = []
    for op, a_start, a_end, b_start, b_end in opcodes:
        block_size = b_end - b_start
        if block_size > 0:
            block_sizes.append(block_size)
        if op in ("replace", "insert"):
            changed_tokens.extend(text_toks[b_start:b_end])
    if block_sizes:
        block_arr = np.array(block_sizes, dtype=float)
        block_probs = block_arr / block_arr.sum()
        block_entropy = -np.sum(block_probs * np.log2(block_probs + 1e-10))
        max_entropy = math.log2(len(block_sizes)) if len(block_sizes) > 1 else 1.0
        structural_signal = max(0.0, min(1.0, block_entropy / (max_entropy + 0.1)))
    else:
        structural_signal = 0.5
    if changed_tokens:
        changed_surp = [_word_surprisal(w) for w in changed_tokens]
        mean_changed_surp = statistics.mean(changed_surp)
        content_gate = max(0.0, min(1.0, (mean_changed_surp - _SURP_MU) / (2.0 * _SURP_SD) + 0.5))
    else:
        content_gate = 0.0
    return structural_signal * content_gate

METRICS = {"structural_diversity_content_gated": structural_diversity_content_gated}

train_failures.anchor: The startup grew quickly in its first year. By December it had hired forty people.
train_failures.more_creative: The startup hit the ground running, and by December forty new faces had crowded into a space built for ten.
train_failures.less_creative: The startup expanded over its first year. By December it employed forty workers at the office.

train_failures.anchor: The movie was long but interesting. The ending surprised most viewers.
train_failures.more_creative: The movie ran long, yet it kept you on the edge of your seat, one quiet reveal after another. The ending landed like a trapdoor no one saw underfoot.
train_failures.less_creative: The movie had a long runtime but held interest throughout. Its conclusion was unexpected to most people who watched it.

train_failures.anchor: She practiced piano every day for years. Eventually she performed at a concert hall.
train_failures.more_creative: Years of daily practice finally paid off, each scale filed down until her fingers stopped thinking. Eventually came the concert hall, and a room holding its breath.
train_failures.less_creative: She practiced piano daily across several years. In time she gave a performance in a concert hall.

train_failures.anchor: The report was late because of technical problems. The team apologized to clients.
train_failures.more_creative: The report slipped past its deadline when the software buckled, sending everyone back to the drawing board. The team wrote to clients, apology first, excuses nowhere.
train_failures.less_creative: The report was delayed due to technical issues. The team sent an apology to its clients afterward.

train_failures.anchor: The lake freezes in winter. Children skate on it when it is safe.

train_failures.less_creative: The lake becomes frozen in winter. Children skate on its surface once it is solid enough.

train_failures.anchor: The bakery sells out of croissants by nine. You have to get there early.
train_failures.more_creative: The croissants are gone by nine, so you learn to show up early. It's worth the alarm.
train_failures.less_creative: Their croissants evanesce ere the ninth hour tolls. One must undertake an early pilgrimage to procure them.

train_failures.anchor: The old man walked slowly through the park this afternoon. He felt surprisingly at peace with himself.
train_failures.more_creative: Ambling the overgrown pathways with deliberate pauses, the weathered wanderer rediscovered the layered quiet of late-afternoon solitude.
train_failures.less_creative: The venerable individual ambulated in leisurely fashion via the recreational green expanse during the afternoon period. A sensation of tranquility was experienced by his consciousness in profound measure.

train_failures.anchor: Cities expand outward when populations increase significantly over time. Buildings gradually replace agricultural land and farmland.

train_failures.less_creative: Cities, somewhat remarkably, expand outward when populations increase continuously. Buildings, in certain cases, replace agricultural land and farmland.
